title: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript working together
learningObjectives: Explain html, css, and javascript working together and create a small runnable JavaScript example.

understand.concept: HTML provides document structure and meaning, CSS controls presentation and layout, and JavaScript adds behaviour. A browser combines these layers to render and update a page. Good projects keep responsibilities clear while allowing the layers to work together.
understand.whyItMatters: Separating responsibilities makes code easier to understand, test, and maintain. JavaScript should not be used to replace semantic HTML or basic CSS layout without a clear reason.
understand.analogy: HTML is the structure, CSS is the visual design, and JavaScript is the interaction that makes the interface respond.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; script loading and JavaScript evaluation follow browser parsing and language rules.

explain.narrative: HTML creates the button and paragraph, CSS defines the highlight class, and JavaScript responds to the click by updating text and class.

examples.code: A structured message.
examples.explanation: HTML creates the button and paragraph, CSS defines the highlight class, and JavaScript responds to the click by updating text and class.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser page or developer console shows the result described in the example.

practise.guidedTask: Build a small card with semantic HTML, a CSS class for appearance, and JavaScript to toggle a visible state. Identify each layer's responsibility.
practise.independentTask: Create a small page with an external or embedded script. Test its execution order and inspect the console for errors.
hints: Keep behaviour separate from semantic markup where practical.
Choose defer, async, or module based on dependencies and ordering.
